strategies.title: [variable-neighborhood-descent] Complete-permutation relocate descent
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: variable-neighborhood-descent  
Replacement scope: Replace the incumbent’s adjacent-swap-only improvement loop after each greedy construction.  
Compute budget: At most 3 descent rounds per constructed schedule; each round tests all adjacent swaps and at most 6 bounded relocation targets per transaction (`i±2`, `i±4`, `i±8`), stopping at the shared deadline. This adds at most roughly `7*n` exact full-schedule evaluations per round, with cache hits eliminating repeats.  
Gain mechanism: The incumbent can only move a transaction several positions through a sequence of individually improving adjacent swaps. A beneficial relocation can require passing through a temporarily worse intermediate ordering, so adjacent descent cannot reach it. Test complete schedules formed by removing transaction `i` and reinserting it at the bounded target position, accept only strict true-cost improvements, then resume adjacent descent. This preserves validity because remove-and-insert preserves every transaction ID exactly once.  

Observed bottleneck: the measured incumbent is strong at 292 but its greedy choices are only repaired by one-edge order changes. Use an identity-permutation fallback before all search and retain the best exact-cost feasible permutation. Expected-gain check: this exposes the precise relocate move `(…,a,b,c,d,x,e,…) -> (…,a,x,b,c,d,e,…)`, which the incumbent cannot accept when one of the required intermediate adjacent swaps is non-improving; evaluation falsifies the hypothesis unless the summed makespan drops below the incumbent’s 292.

strategies.title: [destroy-repair-subsequence] Conflict-sensitive ruin and exact-position repair
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: destroy-repair-subsequence  
Replacement scope: Replace one greedy-start construction plus its local-search phase with a destroy-and-repair phase seeded from the current best complete schedule.  
Compute budget: At most 4 ruin-repair attempts per workload; remove a fixed bounded subset of at most `min(8, max(3, n//8))` transactions; reinsert each removed transaction by evaluating every insertion position in the current partial sequence; perform one adjacent-swap descent pass after repair. Stop immediately at the shared deadline.  
Gain mechanism: Select removed transactions by evaluating the true-cost degradation caused by deleting each transaction from the incumbent schedule and remove the transactions whose deletion gives the largest improvement, breaking ties by transaction ID. This targets precedence choices currently on the critical path without requiring direct access to simulator internals. Rebuild by repeatedly choosing the removed transaction and insertion position that yields the lowest exact partial-sequence cost. Unlike an adjacent exchange, this jointly replaces a mesoscopic subsequence and allows several formerly separated transactions to be reordered together. All candidates remain valid because each repair starts with retained IDs and inserts each removed ID once.  

Observed bottleneck: greedy construction commits early conflict precedences, while adjacent swaps only make one local ordering edit. Preserve the incumbent as fallback and use only exact `get_opt_seq_cost` comparisons for acceptance. Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is simultaneous replacement of the relative order and locations of up to eight critical transactions, unavailable to incumbent adjacent descent; the hypothesis is falsified unless a repair produces a true total makespan below 292.

strategies.title: [prefix-beam-construction] Diverse beam search over transaction prefixes
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: prefix-beam-construction  
Replacement scope: Replace the single-path `greedy(start)` constructor and its fixed first-transaction starts with a bounded beam of distinct partial permutations.  
Compute budget: Six construction rounds per workload; each round uses a beam width of 3 and expands each beam state by at most 10 remaining transactions per depth, for at most `180*n` prefix evaluations per workload before local refinement. Use the existing shared 330-second deadline and return immediately when it expires.  
Gain mechanism: At every depth retain the three lowest true-cost distinct prefixes rather than irrevocably retaining only the cheapest one. Seed each beam with three different transaction IDs, rotating deterministically across rounds. The retained alternatives differ in conflict precedence topology, allowing a prefix that is slightly worse early but avoids a later read/write serialization chain to survive to completion. Finish every beam state to a complete permutation before scoring, and only return the best exact feasible schedule.  

Observed bottleneck: the incumbent samples alternatives at a position but discards every non-winning branch, causing irreversible prefix bias; Context 2’s randomized variants were weaker, so this uses deterministic retained alternatives rather than merely more random starts. Expected-gain check: beam states preserve competing prefix orders that incumbent greedy construction discards at the same depth, and the hypothesis is falsified unless the evaluator observes a total true makespan below 292.

strategies.title: [critical-window-exact] Exact critical-window permutation descent
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: critical-window-exact

Replacement scope: Replace the current bounded adjacent-swap descent phase after destroy-repair with exact permutation optimization of selected contiguous transaction windows.

Compute budget: At most three windows per destroy-repair candidate, each containing four transactions and evaluating at most 24 permutations; perform at most two full passes over the selected windows. This adds at most 144 simulator calls per attempt, with deadline checks before every window and permutation.

Gain mechanism: The observed adjacent-swap refinement only accepts a one-edge move in permutation space. A beneficial reordering of four transactions can require one or more temporarily worsening adjacent swaps and is therefore unreachable from an adjacent local minimum. Select windows centered on the largest-gap positions in the repaired schedule, including beginning, middle, and end regions; hold every transaction outside the window fixed; enumerate all 4! internal orders; and accept the minimum true simulator cost order. This preserves the complete-permutation invariant because it only permutes existing transaction IDs. The incumbent schedule remains available if no window improves it.

The observed bottleneck is that destroy-repair can produce a good global placement whose remaining precedence errors are coupled across several neighboring transactions, while adjacent descent cannot cross a worsening intermediate state; exact local window enumeration directly searches those coupled orderings. Expected-gain check: this mechanism can realize a four-transaction cyclic reorder requiring a worsening first adjacent swap, which the incumbent cannot accept; evaluation falsifies the hypothesis unless the total true makespan falls from 283 to at most 282, corresponding to combined_score \(1000000/(1+282)=3533.5689\), above 3521.1268.

strategies.title: [critical-subset-ordering] Exact mesoscopic critical-subset reorder
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: critical-subset-ordering

Replacement scope: Replace the current choice of only `ruin_count` transactions followed by greedy one-at-a-time reinsertion with a critical-subset phase that retains the current transaction positions but exactly optimizes the relative order of six selected critical transactions.

Compute budget: One selected subset of six transactions per outer attempt; enumerate at most 6! = 720 relative orders, stopping immediately at the deadline. Use at most two outer attempts, and retain the current valid incumbent if the enumeration is incomplete. Expected runtime is bounded by 1,440 cost evaluations per workload call and the existing deadline.

Gain mechanism: Compute deletion impacts exactly as the incumbent already does, select the six largest-impact transactions, locate their six current slots, and test every ordering of those same IDs in those slots while all other transactions remain fixed. This is a mesoscopic subsystem solve rather than a greedy insertion sequence: it jointly changes every pairwise precedence relationship inside the critical set. It avoids reliance on workload internals and remains valid because every candidate is a permutation of exactly `range(workload.num_txns)`.

The observed bottleneck is greedy reinsertion commits the first critical transaction before the interaction effects of later critical transactions are known; exact relative-order enumeration removes that sequential commitment for the conflict-heavy subsystem. Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is simultaneous reversal or interleaving of all six influential transactions while preserving their external contacts, which greedy one-at-a-time repair cannot generally revisit jointly; the hypothesis is falsified unless evaluator total makespan is at most 282.

strategies.title: [regret-insertion-construction] True-cost global regret insertion constructor
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: regret-insertion-construction

Replacement scope: Replace the identity-order initialization and first destroy-repair attempt with a from-scratch construction phase, then use the existing destroy-repair optimizer only on the better of the constructed schedule and identity schedule.

Compute budget: Two deterministic constructions. For each construction, maintain a partial schedule and, at each depth, evaluate every remaining transaction at every insertion position. Choose the transaction whose best insertion is cheapest, breaking ties by the gap between its best and second-best insertion costs so difficult transactions are placed before their good placements disappear. Hard-stop construction at the shared deadline; if interrupted, append unplaced IDs in deterministic order to obtain a valid full permutation. No more than two construction starts and no post-construction iteration increase.

Gain mechanism: The incumbent begins from transaction-ID order, so its later ruin operator must discover long-range beneficial contact topology through limited removal. Global regret insertion constructs the entire contact topology directly from true partial simulator costs: it chooses both the next transaction and its location, while regret protects transactions having only one low-conflict placement. Use two deterministic tie orientations, ascending and descending transaction-ID ties, to expose distinct complete schedules without random-seed dependence. Every partial and completed candidate has unique IDs, and unfinished candidates are completed before any return.

The observed bottleneck is structural: a fixed identity constructor predetermines most noncritical contacts before only a small set is removed, whereas a regret constructor can choose the global arrangement before local optimization begins. Expected-gain check: the construction has the new freedom to place a transaction at its sole low-conflict slot before later placements consume it, a choice unavailable to identity initialization plus limited ruin; evaluation falsifies this structural hypothesis unless total true makespan reaches at most 282.

strategies.title: [paired-ruin-repair] joint two-transaction repair
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: paired-ruin-repair

Replacement scope: Replace the current single-transaction greedy reinsertion loop inside the ruin-repair phase, while retaining the successful regret-insertion constructor and impact-based removal selection.

Compute budget: At most 4 ruin attempts; remove at most 8 transactions as now. For each attempt, jointly place only the two highest-impact removed transactions first, evaluating both pair orders and every legal pair of insertion positions in the retained partial order. Reinsert the remaining removed transactions with the existing single-transaction exact-position rule. Expected evaluation-time effect: bounded additional \(O(n^2)\) simulator calls per ruin attempt, so reserve the same 105-second per-workload cap and stop pair enumeration immediately at the deadline.

Gain mechanism: The incumbent commits to the best location of one removed transaction before seeing the placement of another removed transaction. That cannot represent a coordinated repair where two conflicting transactions must move together, be reversed, or be separated by a particular retained transaction. Jointly selecting pair order and positions introduces this missing two-transaction topology while preserving every unaffected transaction’s relative order. Build a valid partial permutation, enumerate only positions that produce complete unique transaction permutations, retain the incumbent unless the exact true cost improves, and preserve identity as the emergency fallback. Expected-gain check: this is falsifiably successful if the three-workload total makespan falls from 255 to at most 254, which gives \(1{,}000{,}000/(1+254)=3921.5686\), strictly above 3906.25.

strategies.title: [conflict-tournament-construction] pairwise precedence seed followed by exact in
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: conflict-tournament-construction

Replacement scope: Replace one of the two reverse-tie regret constructors, not the repair stage, with a complete structural seed based on pairwise precedence costs followed by exact insertion polishing.

Compute budget: One structural start per workload. Evaluate each unordered transaction pair exactly twice using `get_opt_seq_cost([i, j])` and `get_opt_seq_cost([j, i])`; construct a directed weighted precedence graph where the lower-cost order receives the difference as its edge weight. Produce an initial permutation by deterministic weighted insertion: insert transactions one by one into the position minimizing the total backward edge weight against already placed transactions. Then perform one full true-cost best-insertion pass: remove each transaction in current order and reinsert it at its exact minimum-cost position. Expected evaluation-time effect: \(O(n^2)\) pair evaluations plus one \(O(n^2)\) exact refinement pass, bounded by the constructor’s 48-second reservation; if the deadline arrives, finish with the current complete permutation.

Gain mechanism: The incumbent starts from an empty order and decides the next transaction using the makespan of short partial schedules. It has no explicit representation of which direction each pair’s read/write conflicts prefer. The weighted tournament seed makes every transaction pair contribute a precedence signal before global true-cost polishing, enabling a different basin of complete schedules than either transaction-ID tie direction can create. The output remains a complete permutation by construction; compare its exact full cost to the incumbent and retain only the better valid result. Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is a weighted directed pair-precedence topology, absent from the incumbent’s empty-prefix selection; it passes the evaluator only if the returned total true makespan is at most 254.

strategies.title: [segment-exchange-descent] exact mesoscopic block transposition
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: segment-exchange-descent

Replacement scope: Replace the final adjacent-swap descent after each ruin repair with deterministic block-transposition descent over the repaired full permutation.

Compute budget: At most two accepted block moves per ruin attempt. Enumerate disjoint contiguous blocks of lengths 1 through 3, in increasing left endpoint order, and evaluate swapping their order while retaining internal block order and all surrounding transaction order. Use first strict true-cost improvement, restart enumeration after an accepted move, and stop at the existing deadline. Expected evaluation-time effect: at most 8 accepted/restarted scans total and no new optimizer starts; cap each scan to the first 1,500 legal block pairs if `n` is large.

Gain mechanism: Adjacent swaps can only cross one schedule boundary at a time and are trapped when moving a transaction across a conflicting cluster temporarily increases makespan. A block transposition crosses two boundaries atomically and can relocate a short serially conflicting cluster without exposing those harmful intermediate schedules. It is neither critical-subset permutation search nor ordinary relocate descent because the invariant is preservation of the internal order of both exchanged contiguous schedule segments. Every candidate is made by exchanging disjoint slices of an existing complete permutation, so validity is automatic; exact full cost remains the acceptance criterion. Expected-gain check: this new atomic two-boundary move is unavailable to the incumbent’s adjacent-only descent; it is accepted as an improvement only if evaluation reports total makespan at most 254.
